```{r setup}
library(targets)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
cfg      <- tar_read(config)
data_end <- tar_read(data_end)
rl       <- tar_read(rolling)
re       <- tar_read(roll_eval)
rx       <- tar_read(roll_example)
rd       <- tar_read(readiness)
tm       <- Filter(Negate(is.null), tar_read(timing_region))
codes    <- tar_read(eval_codes)
nm_city  <- tar_read(cities)[, .(URAU_CODE, name)]
fmt <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(x, d = 0) paste0(fmt(100 * x, d), "%")
kbl <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, ...)
rc  <- cfg$rolling
has_roll <- !is.null(rl) && nrow(rl$windows) > 0 && !is.null(re)
PUB <- if (has_roll) re$curve_sets[1] else "Published (Masselot et al.)"
SYS <- if (has_roll) rl$label else rc$label
ap  <- if (has_roll) tail(re$periods, 1) else ""
city_names <- sort(nm_city[URAU_CODE %in% codes, name])
n_ep <- if (has_roll) re$windows[curves == SYS & type == "episode", .N] else 0
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Verdict: `r if (!is.null(rd)) rd$verdict else "not available"`.**
`r if (!is.null(rd)) sprintf("%d of %d pre-specified criteria met (%d of %d core criteria), over %d heatwave episodes in %d cities of %s, %s.", sum(rd$criteria$pass), nrow(rd$criteria), sum(rd$criteria[core == TRUE, pass]), rd$criteria[core == TRUE, .N], n_ep, length(codes), cfg$region_focus, tolower(rd$period)) else ""`
Temperatures are those recorded (ERA5-Land): this validates the
heat-to-deaths part of the system; forecast errors are left to a later
version.
:::

# Introduction

The impact-based system turns daily temperatures into numbers of deaths: for
every city and day it gives the deaths expected without heat, the deaths
expected with the temperatures of that day, the difference (deaths
attributable to heat), a 95% range for each, and a warning when deaths are
expected to exceed what is normal for the season. The temperature-mortality
relation comes from the exposure-response functions of Masselot et al.
[-@masselot2023], **recalibrated every month on the last `r rc$train_years`
years of Istat deaths**, because the published curves (2001-2010 data)
overstate today's heat risk in Italy (companion report on adaptation).

This report asks whether the system is ready to be used: whether, given the
temperatures that actually occurred, its numbers of deaths match the deaths
that were observed, whether its uncertainty ranges contain them as often as
they should, and whether it would have warned of the heatwaves that caused
an abnormal excess of deaths without raising too many false alarms. The
published curves are scored alongside as the reference the system has to
improve on. The scope is the `r length(codes)` cities of `r cfg$region_focus`
(`r paste(city_names, collapse = ", ")`), over every summer for which a
rolling curve exists: 2014-2019 and 2023-`r format(data_end, "%Y")`.

# Methods

## Data

Deaths: Istat daily deaths by comune of residence, aged 20+, summed over the
comuni of each Urban Audit city (official Istat Cities 2021 composition),
up to `r format(data_end, "%d %B %Y")`. Temperatures: daily mean ERA5-Land,
averaged over the grid cells inside each city; the published study's own
series up to 2019, an aligned reconstruction afterwards. City definitions,
checks on deaths and population, and the alignment of the temperature series
are described in full in the companion report; they are the same here.

## Exposure-response curves

**Published curves (reference).** For each city and age group, the published
quadratic B-spline of daily mean temperature (knots at the 10th, 75th and
90th percentiles of the city's 1990-2019 distribution, boundaries at its
minimum and maximum) cumulated over lags 0-21, with its covariance matrix.
For deaths 20+ the five age-specific relative risks are applied to the
baseline of each age group.

**Rolling curves (the system).** For every target month (`r paste(month.abb[rc$target_months], collapse = ", ")`):

1. *Training window:* the last `r rc$train_years` years of days before the
   month (`r if (identical(rc$update, "monthly")) "up to the last day of the previous month" else "up to 31 December of the previous year"`, and never after the last day of data), skipping every day of
   `r paste(range(rc$skip_years), collapse = "-")` and counting back until
   `r rc$train_years` years of days are collected. July 2024, for example, is
   trained on July 2018-December 2019 plus January 2023-June 2024. A target
   whose window would start before the first Istat day (1 January 2011) is not
   predicted, so the first target is May 2014; targets in
   `r paste(range(rc$skip_years), collapse = "-")` are not predicted.
2. *First stage:* in every Italian city, deaths 20+ are modelled with the
   published first-stage model - quasi-Poisson regression, cross-basis of
   temperature (published knots) and lag (natural spline, lags 0-`r cfg$lag_max`,
   `r cfg$lag_nknots` log-spaced knots), day of week, and a natural spline of
   time with `r cfg$df_time_per_year` df per year fitted *separately in each
   contiguous block of the window* (with its own intercept), so that the
   2019-2023 gap does not consume degrees of freedom - and reduced to the
   overall cumulative curve (five coefficients in the published basis).
3. *Second stage:* the city fits are pooled in a multivariate random-effects
   meta-analysis (REML; method of moments, then fixed effect, as fall-backs)
   [@gasparrini2012; @sera2019]; every Italian city with at least
   `r format(rc$min_deaths, big.mark = ",")` deaths in the window enters, and
   every city that needs a curve is fitted whatever its size. Each city takes
   its best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP), which shrinks a noisy city
   towards the pooled curve.
4. *Curve in force:* on a given day the system uses the curve of the latest
   window that ended before that day. Every prediction is therefore made
   with deaths that were available at the time: the evaluation is out of
   sample.

## Minimum mortality temperature

For each curve the minimum mortality temperature (MMT) is found as in the
published study: the log relative risk is evaluated on the city's
temperature percentiles (0.1th to 99.9th) and the MMT is the percentile
temperature with the lowest risk between the `r cfg$mmp_range[1]`th and the
`r cfg$mmp_range[2]`th percentile. The relative risk is centred on it,
RR(MMT) = 1. Each rolling curve has its own MMT, so it can move from month to
month; for the published curves each age group has its own. Days at or above
the MMT are *heat days*; days below carry the cold side of the curve, which
is not part of heat deaths.

## Deaths expected without heat

For every city and age group, the baseline $B_t$ is a quasi-Poisson model of
daily deaths with day of the week, a natural spline of time
(`r cfg$baseline_trend_df_per_year` df per year) and
`r cfg$baseline_harmonics` annual sine-cosine pair, fitted only on reference
days: outside `r paste(month.abb[cfg$baseline_exclude_months], collapse = ", ")`
(influenza) and not within `r cfg$baseline_hot_lag` days after a day at or above
the MMT. `r if (isTRUE(cfg$baseline_cold_offset)) "The published cold relative risk enters as an offset on reference days, so $B_t$ is the number of deaths expected at the MMT." else ""`
It is fitted separately for 2011-2019 and for 2023 onwards. Groups with fewer
than `r cfg$baseline_min_daily` deaths a day use the 20+ model times their
share of deaths.

## Predicted deaths

With $RR_t$ the relative risk of day $t$'s temperature (centred on the MMT):

- deaths expected with that day's temperature: $E_t = B_t \, RR_t$;
- heat deaths: $P = \sum_t B_t (RR_t - 1)$ over the heat days of a window;
- observed heat deaths, against which $P$ is checked: $X = O - B$, observed
  minus expected without heat, over the same window.

The cumulative relative risk carries the effect of a day's temperature over
the following `r cfg$lag_max` days and is assigned to that day, as in the
published attribution.

## Uncertainty

Three sources are combined by simulation (`r format(cfg$nsim, big.mark = ",")` draws):

- **curve:** coefficient vectors drawn from the multivariate normal of the
  BLUP (rolling) or the published simulations (published), the MMT held at
  its point estimate;
- **baseline level:** one log-normal multiplier per draw, with the standard
  deviation of the baseline model's predictions, shared by all the days of a
  window (an error in the level of $B$ is common to neighbouring days);
- **counts:** observed deaths drawn as negative binomial around each draw's
  $E$, with the overdispersion $\phi$ of the baseline model (variance =
  $\phi \times$ mean).

The *confidence interval* of $P$ uses the first two; the *prediction
interval* of the observed deaths $O$ uses all three, and is the grey band of
the app (for a 7-day mean, the draws are averaged over the 7 days before
taking quantiles).

## Episodes and summers

A **heatwave episode** is a spell of at least `r cfg$hw_min_days` days in
`r paste(month.abb[range(cfg$warm_months)], collapse = "-")` with daily mean
temperature at or above the city's `r cfg$hw_pct`th percentile of 1990-2019,
spells separated by at most `r cfg$hw_max_gap` day being merged; its window
runs to `r cfg$tail_days` days after the last hot day, to include delayed
deaths. `r if (!isFALSE(cfg$hw_merge_windows)) sprintf("Episodes are then merged into **whole heatwaves**: when an episode starts within the window of the previous one (or the day after it ends), the two are one heatwave, scored over a single window from the first hot day to %d days after the last. No day, and no death, belongs to two windows, and a hot period broken by a few cooler days is judged as the one event it is.", cfg$tail_days) else ""`
Every episode is scored in its own city: the system is used city by city. **Whole summers** (June-September) are scored as well, since they do
not depend on the episode definition. Episodes are defined on temperature
only, never on deaths.

## Significant excess, observed and forecast

For each episode window, the **no-heat range** is the 95% prediction
interval of deaths if there were no heat: $B$ with its level uncertainty and
negative binomial noise. Then:

- a **significant excess was observed** when $O$ is above the upper end of
  the no-heat range;
- a **significant excess was forecast** (a warning) when the deaths the
  curves expect, $E = \sum_t B_t RR_t$, are above that same upper end.

## Calibration

Across episodes (and, separately, summers):

- *ratio of totals:* $\sum X / \sum P$, 1 if the system predicts as many heat
  deaths as were observed;
- *calibration slope:* weighted least squares of $X$ on $P$ through the
  origin, weights $1/\mathrm{Var}(O)$; below 1 the system over-predicts, and
  more so for larger episodes;
- *correlation* of $X$ and $P$, and *mean absolute error* per episode;
- *coverage:* share of episodes whose observed deaths fall inside the 95%
  prediction interval (95% expected);

overall, for **large episodes** (published prediction in the top
`r pct(1 - rc$large_quantile)` - a function of temperatures and baseline only,
so the same episodes for both sets of curves and no selection on the
outcome), and for **episodes with a significant observed excess** (selected on
the outcome: chance pushes these up, so any set of curves looks a little low
on them; useful to compare the two sets, not as an absolute measure).

## Warning skill

Warnings and observed excesses form a 2 x 2 table over all episodes: hits
($a$), false alarms ($b$), misses ($c$), correct negatives ($d$). Scores
[@jolliffe2012; @wilks2019]:

- probability of detection $\mathrm{POD} = a/(a+c)$;
- false alarm ratio $\mathrm{FAR} = b/(a+b)$;
- critical success index $\mathrm{CSI} = a/(a+b+c)$;
- frequency bias $(a+b)/(a+c)$, 1 when there are as many warnings as events;
- Peirce skill score $\mathrm{PSS} = a/(a+c) - b/(b+d)$;
- Heidke skill score $\mathrm{HSS} = 2(ad - bc)/[(a+c)(c+d) + (a+b)(b+d)]$,
  0 for chance, 1 for perfect.

## Timing check

Within each city and summer, daily excess deaths and temperature (both centred
on their summer means) are correlated with temperature shifted by -10 to +10
days. Deaths must follow temperature (peak at 0 to +2 days); a negative peak
would reveal a date misalignment between deaths and temperatures.

## Baseline audit

Observed heat deaths are measured against the baseline, $X = O - B$, so the
level of $B$ decides them: a baseline 3% too high removes 3% of all deaths of
a window from $X$, often most of the heat signal. Two checks:

- **Cool days.** On the baseline's reference days (not hot, not just after
  heat) the model expects $B$ times the cold relative risk; observed /
  expected there should be 1. Spring and autumn days dominate the fit and
  stay close to 1 by construction; summer reference days are few and lie
  between hot spells, so a baseline whose summer level is off shows up there.
  A ratio below 1 means $B$ is too high in summer and $X$ too low. Summer
  reference days are themselves part of the fit, so the check is weak: a
  baseline can pass it and still be off by a few percent in summer.
- **Alternative baselines.** The baseline is refitted with alternative,
  equally defensible choices
  (`r paste(names(cfg$baseline_variants), collapse = "; ")`) and the whole
  evaluation is repeated with the same curves. The spread of the results is
  how much of them belongs to the yardstick rather than to the curves; this
  is the stronger of the two checks.

## Readiness criteria

Fixed before the results were produced (configuration `readiness`); the
verdict is "ready" when all are met, "ready with caveats" when only non-core
ones fail, "not ready" when a core one fails.

```{r criteria-def}
kbl(rbindlist(lapply(cfg$readiness, function(r) data.table(
  Criterion = r$label, `Accepted range` = sprintf("%g to %g", r$lo, r$hi),
  Core = fifelse(r$core, "yes", "no")))))
```

# Results

## Episodes and timing

```{r ep-summary}
if (has_roll) {
  w <- re$windows[curves == SYS & type %in% c("episode", "summer")]
  kbl(w[, .(Windows = .N, Cities = uniqueN(URAU_CODE),
            `Observed deaths` = fmt(sum(O), 0), `Expected without heat` = fmt(sum(B), 0),
            `Observed heat deaths` = fmt(sum(X), 0),
            `With significant excess` = sum(obs_sig, na.rm = TRUE)),
          by = .(Period = period, Type = type)],
      caption = "Windows scored (only those with a rolling curve in force on every day)")
}
```

```{r timing, fig.height=3.2}
if (length(tm)) {
  cc <- rbindlist(lapply(names(tm), function(p) cbind(period = p, tm[[p]]$ccf)))
  pk <- cc[, .SD[which.max(r)], by = period]
  ggplot(cc, aes(lag, r, colour = period)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_line() + geom_point(data = pk, size = 2.5) +
    labs(x = "Days by which deaths follow temperature", y = "Correlation", colour = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

`r if (length(tm)) sprintf("Deaths follow temperature: the correlation peaks at %s.", paste(sprintf("%+d days (%s)", pk$lag, pk$period), collapse = " and ")) else ""`

```{r audit-city, fig.height=4.5}
}
```

```{r audit-numbers}
aud_txt <- ""
if (!is.null(ba)) {
  cs <- ba$cool_pooled[baseline == levels(baseline)[1] & season == "Summer (Jun-Sep)"]

}
```

## Calibration of predicted heat deaths

```{r calibration, results='asis'}
if (has_roll) {
  cl <- re$calibration
  print(kbl(cl[, .(Period = period, Windows = fifelse(type == "episode", "Episodes", "Summers"),
                   Subset = subset, Curves = curves, N = n,
                   Observed = fmt(observed, 0), Predicted = fmt(predicted, 0),
                   `Obs / pred` = fmt(ratio),
                   Slope = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", fmt(slope), fmt(lo), fmt(hi)),
                   r = fmt(r), MAE = fmt(mae, 1), `95% PI coverage` = pct(coverage_95))],
            caption = sprintf("Observed vs predicted heat deaths (slope 1 = calibrated). Large episodes: published prediction above %s deaths.",
                              fmt(re$large_threshold, 1))))
}
```

```{r cal-numbers}
if (has_roll) {
  g <- function(sub, cur) re$calibration[period == ap & subset == sub & type == "episode" & curves == cur]
  pa <- g("All windows", PUB); sa <- g("All windows", SYS)
  pl <- g("Large episodes", PUB); sl_ <- g("Large episodes", SYS)
  ok_num <- nrow(pa) && nrow(sa); ok_lg <- nrow(pl) && nrow(sl_)
}
```

`r if (has_roll && ok_num) sprintf("Over %s, the system predicts %s heat deaths in the episodes against %s observed (ratio %s, slope %s); the published curves predict %s (ratio %s). %s of the episodes fall inside the system's 95%% prediction interval.", if (ap == "All periods") "all the years scored" else ap, fmt(sa$predicted, 0), fmt(sa$observed, 0), fmt(sa$ratio), fmt(sa$slope), fmt(pa$predicted, 0), fmt(pa$ratio), pct(sa$coverage_95)) else ""`
`r if (has_roll && ok_lg) sprintf("On large episodes the ratio is %s for the system and %s for the published curves (mean absolute error %s and %s deaths per episode).", fmt(sl_$ratio), fmt(pl$ratio), fmt(sl_$mae, 1), fmt(pl$mae, 1)) else ""`

The chart keeps the episodes with a significant observed excess, the ones a
warning system exists for.

```{r scatter, fig.height=5.5}
if (has_roll) {
  w <- re$windows[type == "episode" & obs_sig == TRUE]
  w[, curves := factor(curves, re$curve_sets)]
  sl <- re$calibration[period == ap & type == "episode" & subset == "Episodes with significant excess"]
  ggplot(w, aes(P, X)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
    geom_abline(colour = "grey40", linetype = 2) +
    geom_abline(data = sl, aes(slope = slope, intercept = 0), colour = "firebrick") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pi_lo - B, ymax = pi_hi - B), colour = "grey80", width = 0) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = size), alpha = .8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Large = "firebrick", Other = "grey40")) +
    facet_wrap(~ curves, nrow = 1) +
    labs(x = "Predicted heat deaths", y = "Observed heat deaths (O - B)", colour = "Episode",
         subtitle = "Dashed: perfect calibration; red: fitted slope; bars: 95% prediction range") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r largest}
if (has_roll) {
  w <- merge(re$windows[type == "episode"], nm_city, by = "URAU_CODE")
  pub <- w[curves == PUB, .(period, id, name, start, end, O, B, X, P_pub = P, sig = obs_sig)]
  sys <- w[curves == SYS, .(period, id, P_sys = P, lo = pi_lo - B, hi = pi_hi - B, in_pi)]
  top <- merge(pub, sys, by = c("period", "id"))[order(-P_pub)][seq_len(min(15, .N))]
  kbl(top[, .(name, start, end, fmt(O, 0), fmt(B, 0), fmt(X, 0), fmt(P_pub, 0), fmt(P_sys, 0),
              sprintf("%s to %s", fmt(lo, 0), fmt(hi, 0)), in_pi, fifelse(sig, "yes", "no"))],
      col.names = c("City", "Start", "End", "Observed", "Expected without heat",
                    "Observed heat deaths", "Published", "System", "System: 95% range",
                    "In range", "Significant excess"),
      caption = "Largest episodes: predicted heat deaths and the system's 95% range for the observed ones")
}
```

## Daily prediction band

For every summer day of `r if (!is.null(rx)) rx$city else "the example city"`,
the grey band is the 95% prediction interval of the system; days outside it
are marked. A calibrated band leaves about 2.5% of days on each side.

```{r band, fig.height=11}
if (!is.null(rx)) {
  d <- copy(rx$data)
  d[, flag := factor(flag, c("above", "below", "within"),
                     c("Above the band", "Below the band", "Within"))]
  share <- d[, .(above = mean(flag == "Above the band"), below = mean(flag == "Below the band"))]
  ggplot(d, aes(date)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pi_lo, ymax = pi_hi), fill = "grey80") +
    geom_line(aes(y = B, colour = "Expected without heat"), linewidth = .5, linetype = 2) +
    geom_line(aes(y = pred_pub, colour = "Published curves"), linewidth = .5) +
    geom_line(aes(y = pred, colour = "System (rolling curves)"), linewidth = .7) +
    geom_point(aes(y = observed, shape = flag, alpha = flag == "Within"), size = 1.1) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = .35, `FALSE` = 1), guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`Above the band` = 17, `Below the band` = 25, Within = 16)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`Expected without heat` = "steelblue",
                                   `Published curves` = "firebrick",
                                   `System (rolling curves)` = "#1B7837")) +
    facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Deaths per day (20+)", colour = NULL, shape = "Observed",
         subtitle = sprintf("Days above the band: %s; below: %s", pct(share$above, 1),
                            pct(share$below, 1))) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

## Warnings

```{r matrix, results='asis'}
if (has_roll && !is.null(re$warnings)) {
  for (cs in re$curve_sets) {
    x <- re$warnings[period == ap & curves == cs]
    if (!nrow(x)) next
    m <- data.table(` ` = c("Excess forecast", "No excess forecast"),
                    `Excess observed` = c(x$hits, x$misses),
                    `No excess observed` = c(x$false_alarms, x$correct_negatives))
    print(kbl(m, caption = sprintf("%s: %d episodes", cs, x$n)))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```

```{r scores}
if (has_roll && !is.null(re$warnings))
  kbl(re$warnings[, .(Period = period, Curves = curves, Episodes = n, Hits = hits,
                      `False alarms` = false_alarms, Misses = misses,
                      `Correct negatives` = correct_negatives, POD = fmt(pod), FAR = fmt(far),
                      CSI = fmt(csi), Bias = fmt(bias), PSS = fmt(pss), HSS = fmt(hss))],
      caption = "Warning scores")
```

```{r episodes-list}
if (has_roll) {
  w <- merge(re$windows[type == "episode"], nm_city, by = "URAU_CODE")
  oc <- function(o, f) fifelse(o & f, "Hit", fifelse(o & !f, "Missed",
                         fifelse(!o & f, "False alarm", "")))
  pub <- w[curves == PUB, .(period, id, name, start, end, O, nh_hi, X, obs_sig, P_pub = P,
                            out_pub = oc(obs_sig, fc_sig))]
  sys <- w[curves == SYS, .(period, id, P_sys = P, lo = pi_lo - B, hi = pi_hi - B,
                            out_sys = oc(obs_sig, fc_sig))]
  wl <- merge(pub, sys, by = c("period", "id"))[obs_sig | out_pub != "" | out_sys != ""][
    order(start, name)]
  kbl(wl[, .(name, start, end, fmt(O, 0), fmt(nh_hi, 0), fmt(X, 0), fifelse(obs_sig, "yes", "no"),
             fmt(P_pub, 0), out_pub, fmt(P_sys, 0), sprintf("%s to %s", fmt(lo, 0), fmt(hi, 0)),
             out_sys)],
      col.names = c("City", "Start", "End", "Observed", "No-heat upper bound",
                    "Observed heat deaths", "Significant excess", "Published",
                    "Published: warning", "System", "System: 95% range", "System: warning"),
      caption = "Every episode with a significant excess observed or forecast by either set of curves")
}
```

# Discussion

## Is the system ready?

```{r readiness}
if (!is.null(rd))
  kbl(rd$criteria[, .(Criterion = criterion, `Accepted range` = range,
                      Core = fifelse(core, "yes", "no"), System = system,
                      `Published (reference)` = published,
                      Met = fifelse(pass, "yes", "**no**"))],
      caption = sprintf("Readiness criteria, %s", tolower(rd$period)))
```

```{r disc}
fails <- if (!is.null(rd)) rd$criteria[pass == FALSE] else data.table()
```

**Verdict: `r if (!is.null(rd)) rd$verdict else "n/a"`.**
`r if (!is.null(rd) && !nrow(fails)) "Every criterion is met: on recorded temperatures the system predicts the heat deaths of the region's heatwaves without systematic bias, its 95% ranges contain the observed deaths about as often as they should, and it warns of abnormal excess with few misses and few false alarms." else if (!is.null(rd)) sprintf("Criteria not met: %s.", paste(sprintf("%s (%s, accepted %s)", tolower(fails$criterion), fails$system, fails$range), collapse = "; ")) else ""`
`r if (!is.null(rd) && has_roll && ok_num) sprintf("Against the published curves, the system moves the ratio of observed to predicted heat deaths from %s to %s.", fmt(pa$ratio), fmt(sa$ratio)) else ""`

**What this validation covers.** The chain from temperature to deaths, with
the temperatures that occurred, scored out of sample (every curve uses only
deaths available before the month it predicts) over
`r if (!is.null(re)) paste(head(re$periods, -1), collapse = " and ") else ""`,
with fixed criteria. It does not cover the temperature forecast: in operation
the system will receive forecasts 1-7 days ahead, whose errors (a warm bias
on hot days, growing with lead time) add to the ranges above. That is the
next validation step.

`r aud_txt`

**Known limitations.**

- *Depletion within long episodes.* The curves have no memory of how long
  the heat has lasted; in long episodes deaths can peak before the hottest
  days because the most vulnerable die first. Over-prediction concentrated in
  long episodes points here.
- *Baseline level.* Observed heat deaths are measured against the baseline,
  whose level is anchored by the published cold effect; a few percent of
  error in it moves observed heat deaths by much more, in either direction.
- *Few events.* `r n_ep` episodes in `r length(codes)` cities; small cities
  contribute few deaths each, and the scores have wide uncertainty.
- *First post-COVID windows* mix 2017-2019 with the first months of 2023 and
  the mortality deficit that followed the pandemic.

**Recommendations.** `r if (!is.null(rd) && rd$verdict != "Not ready") "Use the rolling curves, not the published ones, for operational numbers; report the 95% range with every number; and repeat this validation each year with the new Istat release, before each summer, adding the forecast step." else "Do not use the numbers operationally until the core criteria are met; investigate the failing criteria first (depletion in long episodes and the baseline level are the first suspects)."`
